authoritative_source: docs/audit/FINDINGS.md — if this file disagrees, FINDINGS.md wins

rules.take: a whole batch id, not individual findings — batches are grouped by files touched
rules.baseline: parallel lanes must NOT touch scripts/findings-baseline.txt; it is a ceiling, not an exact match. One reconciliation commit at the end.

run-last.name: verify-and-close
run-last.note: ledger-only writes; collides with every lane by construction

run-alone.name: vestigial-code
run-alone.note: deleting dead code while other lanes add code is how you delete something that just became live

findings.title: The bundle claim has no crash/exception/race recovery: `bundle.state:'running'` can stick forever, and a raced outcome write loses the record of a fired deploy
findings.expected_result: A throwing `runBundle` reaches a terminal `bundle` state instead of leaving `running`; the outcome's AUDIT ENTRY lands even when the request row refuses the update (a cancel won), because a fired deploy is a fact and not a state transition; the caller gets a specific code, not CHAIN_CONTENTION with nothing written.

findings.title: Cancel can race an in-flight bundle: the change applies but the request reads CANCELLED
findings.expected_result: A cancel committed during a bundle can no longer produce `CANCELLED` on a request whose change applied: either the cancel refuses while a live claim exists, or the timeline records both truthfully. Decide which, and say why in the fix entry.

findings.title: Trigger failure after a landed commit: honest-but-dead-end half state, and spawn timeouts are indistinguishable from exit-1
findings.expected_result: A trigger failure after a landed commit stops being a dead end: the request reaches a state with an exit, and a spawn TIMEOUT is distinguishable from `exit 1` in the recorded evidence.

findings.title: The bundle "claim" is not a mutual-exclusion, and a crashed bundle wedges the request at `running`
findings.expected_result: VERIFY, DO NOT RE-FIX. Both defects look closed already — ERR-11 made the claim guard `eventSeq` (which the claim advances), and ERR-2 added the lease + takeover. Confirm against the code, add a regression test if none pins it, then close with evidence. If any part survives, fix only that part.

findings.title: `executor.replan()` failures are an unmodeled halt: unbounded silent retry, and they abort the rest of the project's due list
findings.expected_result: `executor.replan()` failure is a modelled outcome, not an unbounded silent retry, and one project's failure no longer aborts the rest of the due list.

findings.title: `TerraformExecutor.init()` caches a rejected promise: one transient init failure bricks the executor until restart
findings.expected_result: One transient `init()` failure no longer bricks the executor until restart — the rejected promise is not cached, and a retry can succeed.

findings.title: Stuck `APPLYING` after a worker crash has no reclaim or operator path
findings.expected_result: VERIFY FIRST: API-2's `APPLY_LEASE_MS` + halt-on-expiry, plus cancel accepting the halt statuses, may already close this. Confirm the operator path end to end; close with evidence, or fix only the remaining gap.

findings.title: Scheduler tick re-scans every project's full request collection every minute
findings.expected_result: The tick stops re-scanning every project's full request collection every minute. Needs an index or a due-set the write path maintains — a design decision, not a loop tweak.

findings.title: Freeze-held `kind:'now'` requests dead-end in AWAITING_DEPLOY_APPROVAL after the freeze lifts
findings.expected_result: A freeze-held `kind:'now'` request has a defined path once the freeze lifts, instead of dead-ending in AWAITING_DEPLOY_APPROVAL.

findings.title: Store rows are not validated against the schemas on load: corrupt-but-parseable state is accepted silently
findings.expected_result: Corrupt-but-parseable rows stop loading silently. WARNING: the wrong shim fails a BOOT, not a test (see R-41) — design the legacy-passthrough against real stored shapes, and make refusing loud and specific about which row.

findings.title: Map key concatenation with a space separator is aliasable in principle; client-controlled bytes reach PKs unconstrained
findings.expected_result: Client-controlled bytes can no longer reach a PK unconstrained, and the space-separated map key is no longer aliasable in principle. Security-relevant; assume an adversarial id.

findings.title: No format/version marker in the snapshot file; migration rests entirely on convention
findings.expected_result: The snapshot carries a format/version marker, so a future migration does not rest on convention. Must stay readable by the current loader.

findings.title: Store-seam divergences from the DynamoDB semantics it mirrors
findings.expected_result: Each named seam divergence from DynamoDB is either fixed or documented as deliberate with the reason. A seam that quietly differs makes every local test a lie about production.

findings.title: Seam-fidelity gaps between MemoryStore and the promised DynamoDB semantics
findings.expected_result: As API-17 — batch them; they are the same list from two reports.

findings.title: Every authenticated request triggers a full-store snapshot write; snapshot serialization is synchronous O(store) on the event loop
findings.expected_result: Snapshot serialization stops being synchronous O(store) on the event loop. PR #6 coalesced the WRITES; the serialize step itself still blocks. Note R-32: sequential write latency is still O(store size).

findings.title: Per-project audit chain head serializes all writes and surfaces contention as user-facing 409s after one retry
findings.expected_result: Chain-head contention stops surfacing as user-facing 409s after one retry. The chain is the product's evidence store — a fix that drops entries under load is worse than the 409.

findings.title: Nothing in the store is ever purged: sessions, idempotency markers, and the audit chain grow forever (and every byte is re-serialized per request)
findings.expected_result: A retention story exists for sessions, idempotency markers and the chain. RETENTION OF AN AUDIT CHAIN IS A PRODUCT DECISION, not a cleanup task — state the policy explicitly and get it agreed before implementing.

findings.title: Admin audit "pagination" materializes and re-sorts the whole chain per page; cursor lookup is a linear scan
findings.expected_result: Admin audit paging stops materializing and re-sorting the whole chain per page, and the cursor lookup stops being a linear scan. Same family as PERF-3 (done) — reuse its cursor semantics.

batches.title: Shared-contract layer & the two domain implementations

findings.title: The backend depends on frontend-package internals; the shared-contract layer is a path alias plus a hand-synced copy
findings.expected_result: A real shared package replaces the `@app-lib` path alias + hand-synced `planSummary` copy, installed by both CI jobs. HAZARD: a zod VALUE import through the alias silently collapses the api's types to `unknown` in CI — that is why the copy exists. Until the package lands, an allowlist lint + a copy-parity test is the acceptable partial.

findings.title: The governance domain is implemented twice (server + browser mock) with acknowledged behavioral divergence
findings.expected_result: The mock's surface shrinks toward 'the http client over an in-browser toy store', and the mock-vs-api behavioural gaps are enumerated in ONE table instead of scattered comments. Note ARCH-7 already moved the status vocabulary into the shared seam — follow that shape.

findings.title: Two sources of truth for the catalog: the server validates against the image-baked catalog, the SPA renders the per-project uploaded one
findings.expected_result: Submit-time operation resolution stops disagreeing with what the SPA renders. Decide which catalog is authoritative per project and write it into DOMAIN-MODEL; a digest pin at submit is the alternative.

findings.title: App `DriftProposal` type does not match the wire: `importPayload` has a different shape, and top-level `arn`/`tfType` are mock-only
findings.expected_result: The app's `DriftProposal` type matches the wire. Decide which side is authoritative for `importPayload` and the mock-only `arn`/`tfType` before changing either.

batches.title: Process lifecycle, container and operator surface

findings.title: No process-level failure handling: no graceful shutdown, no rejection/exception handlers, npm-as-PID-1
findings.expected_result: The api is not `npm` as PID 1; SIGTERM is handled; rejection/exception handlers exist and do the right thing. PARTIAL ALREADY: OPS-2 installed handlers and CONC-7 added SIGTERM/SIGINT lock release — build on those, and note R-16 (neither process error handler exits).

findings.title: No graceful shutdown: `npm` as PID 1, no SIGTERM handling, default 10 s grace on the api
findings.expected_result: As ERR-8 — the same defect from the ops report. Fix once, close both.

findings.title: Plain `compose up` (including every self-update cycle) silently strips the armed overlay
findings.expected_result: A plain `compose up` can no longer silently strip the armed overlay, including on every self-update cycle. The fix shape is contested: refuse, warn, or make arming sticky — pick one and justify it.

findings.title: No HTTP request logging and no request IDs anywhere in the api
findings.expected_result: Request logging and request IDs exist. IN A GOVERNANCE PRODUCT THIS IS A PRIVACY SURFACE: decide what must never be logged (params, plan text, tokens) before adding the logger, and reuse `redact.ts`.

findings.title: Project deregistration leaves orphaned satellite rows; a reused id inherits the previous tenant's state
findings.expected_result: Deregistration no longer leaves orphaned satellite rows, and a reused project id cannot inherit the previous tenant's state. Treat as a cross-tenant data-leak class, not a cleanup task.

findings.title: v1 migration writes rows that violate the store schemas, including an `id`≠`username` shape that breaks session resolution
findings.expected_result: The v1 migration stops writing schema-violating rows; the `id` != `username` shape that breaks session resolution is corrected, with a path for rows already written.

findings.title: apiSession role resolution falls back to another scope's role when the user has no binding on the active project
findings.expected_result: Role resolution never falls back to another scope's role when the user has no binding on the active project. Fail closed — this is an authz fail-open.

findings.title: Crash between the version-row transact and the file write leaves an activatable orphan row in the upload lane
findings.expected_result: A crash between the version-row transact and the file write can no longer leave an activatable orphan row.

findings.title: A dangling idempotency marker makes its key permanently unusable
findings.expected_result: A dangling idempotency marker no longer makes its key permanently unusable.

findings.title: Legitimize endpoint mints unlimited duplicate engineer requests for the same digest
findings.expected_result: The legitimize endpoint stops minting unlimited duplicate engineer requests for one digest.

batches.title: CI trust: can the gates actually fail?

findings.title: PG-5's secret heuristic misses the most common real-world shapes, and its designated backstop is dead in CI
findings.expected_result: PG-5 catches the common real-world secret shapes, and its designated backstop actually runs in CI. THE CLASS: a check that cannot run must be indistinguishable from nothing, never from a pass (this session hit exactly that — PG-9 skipped locally with no gitleaks and a token-shaped literal reached CI).

findings.title: Whether the api's live parity/integration suites run in CI depends on unpinned runner-preinstalled toolchains; nothing asserts they ran
findings.expected_result: Whether the live parity/integration suites ran is asserted, not inferred from an unpinned preinstalled toolchain. `CCP_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1` (TEST-4) is the established shape — extend it.

findings.title: The smoke proves boot + serve, not the system's function; PR runs of it are triggered by any `ccp/**` docs change
findings.expected_result: The smoke asserts the system's function, not just boot+serve, and stops being triggered by any `ccp/**` docs change. What it should assert is the design question.

findings.title: The recurring data lane keeps the silent-skip gate its own sibling workflow documents as a trap
findings.expected_result: The recurring data lane stops keeping the silent-skip gate its own sibling workflow documents as a trap.

findings.title: release-images publishes on any tag with no quality gate, mutable version stamping, and an unconditional `latest`
findings.expected_result: release-images gets a quality gate, immutable version stamping, and a conditional `latest`. Release safety — a wrong fix ships a bad image under a good tag.

findings.title: The OpenAPI "parity test" is string containment, not parity
findings.expected_result: The OpenAPI parity test becomes real conformance, not string containment. Designing what conformance means here is the work.

findings.title: OpenAPI contract test is substring matching, not conformance
findings.expected_result: As ARCH-14 — same defect, two reports. Fix once.

findings.title: No code-coverage measurement anywhere; `coverage.test.ts` is not code coverage
findings.expected_result: Code coverage is measured. The thresholds and what they gate are a policy call; `coverage.test.ts` is not code coverage and should be renamed so the next reader is not misled.

findings.title: plan-check R1 structurally vetoes every legitimate plan for a `local.`-targeted foreach op
findings.expected_result: plan-check R1 stops structurally vetoing every legitimate plan for a `local.`-targeted foreach op. WARNING: this is a SAFETY GATE — a loosening that is too broad is a silent security regression, so pin the newly-accepted shapes with fixtures.

findings.title: `moved_block` writes invalid or duplicate-resource HCL at exit 0: no identifier validation, no destination-collision check, no dangling-reference handling
findings.expected_result: `moved_block` no longer writes invalid or duplicate-resource HCL at exit 0: identifiers are validated, destination collisions are refused, dangling references are handled.

findings.title: Duplicated literal-object token-walkers (edit vs driftpropose) have already diverged in behavior
findings.expected_result: The two literal-object token-walkers (edit vs driftpropose) stop diverging. They ALREADY have — reconciling means deciding which behaviour is correct, not merging the code.

findings.title: Golden coverage runs against forked fixture manifests, not the shipped catalog; comment-bearing fixtures are absent
findings.expected_result: Golden coverage runs against the SHIPPED catalog, not forked fixture manifests, and comment-bearing fixtures exist. This is the can-it-fail class (L-1).

findings.title: Shipped catalog op `waf-add-ip-set-entry` can never execute (exit 1 internal error); the corrected manifest exists only in test fixtures
findings.expected_result: `waf-add-ip-set-entry` executes, and the corrected manifest lives in the shipped catalog rather than only in test fixtures. Batch with CTL-11 — same root cause.

findings.title: `pr-prepare`'s UNAPPROVED gate accepts any non-empty approvals list without checking `decision`
findings.expected_result: `pr-prepare`'s UNAPPROVED gate checks `decision`, not merely a non-empty approvals list. Security gate.

findings.title: statediff's managed-set match assumes Terraform state `id` equals the discovery id; false-positive findings for id-divergent types (concrete: `aws_volume_attachment`)
findings.expected_result: statediff stops assuming Terraform state `id` equals the discovery id, so id-divergent types (e.g. `aws_volume_attachment`) stop producing false-positive findings.

findings.title: Committed schemadump artifacts are not reproducible via the documented `gen.sh` pipeline; generated-catalog staleness detection is entirely manual
findings.expected_result: Committed schemadump artifacts are reproducible via the documented `gen.sh`, and staleness detection is mechanical rather than manual. NOTE: IMP-4 (done) added a self-check that REFUSES TO WRITE on anchor mismatch — extend that discipline, and read its lesson about a field-name typo producing a uniform zero.

findings.title: Coverage-sweep family granularity marks undiscoverable resources as "covered" (documented, but with a concrete silent case)
findings.expected_result: Coverage-sweep family granularity stops marking undiscoverable resources as covered. IMP-4's family matcher is the adjacent code and was subtle — read it first.

findings.title: Submit-path full scans: rate-limit check and feasibility each re-scan whole collections per submission
findings.expected_result: The submit path stops re-scanning whole collections per submission for the rate-limit and feasibility checks. Needs an index or a maintained counter — and NOTE the counter must stay correct under the concurrency CONC-12 describes.

findings.title: Upload ingest does 4+ full canonical-JSON passes over the 16 MiB bundle synchronously on the event loop
findings.expected_result: Upload ingest stops doing 4+ full canonical-JSON passes over a 16 MiB bundle synchronously on the event loop.

findings.title: `transactWithAudit` conflates a caller's domain guard failure with chain contention, producing dead error paths and mislabeled conflicts
findings.expected_result: `transactWithAudit` stops conflating a caller's domain guard failure with chain contention. NOTE: this session's CONC-9 fix leans on the current behaviour (a guarded write is refused rather than replayed) — do not break that property while separating the error paths.

findings.title: Conditional-write collisions inside `transactWithAudit` surface as the wrong error
findings.expected_result: As CONC-15 — the same defect from the API report. Fix once, close both.

findings.title: The store-backed submit rate limiter is check-then-insert: concurrent submits breach both caps
findings.expected_result: The store-backed submit rate limiter stops being check-then-insert, so concurrent submits cannot breach both caps.

findings.title: Concurrent first-boot settlement can escape its own race handling and 500 early requests
findings.expected_result: Concurrent first-boot settlement stops escaping its own race handling and 500ing early requests.

findings.title: No route-level concurrency/race tests; store-level concurrency only
findings.expected_result: Route-level concurrency/race tests exist. THE PATTERN IS NOW IN THE REPO: `test/sessionRevokeRace.test.ts` and `test/pendingChangeCas.test.ts` use a store wrapper that commits a competing write between the read and the write. Choosing WHICH races to pin is the judgment.

findings.title: Single-process, single-file scaling ceiling with in-process singletons the planned DynamoDB path would silently break
findings.expected_result: The single-process in-process singletons stop being ones the planned DynamoDB path would silently break. Name each one and say what it becomes.

findings.title: Arming-flag sprawl with no whole-config validation
findings.expected_result: Arming-flag sprawl gets whole-config validation, so a half-armed deployment is refused at boot rather than discovered at the first click.

findings.title: Api-mode submit gates read the advisory localStorage settings, not the server's — the freeze preview is dead and a stale local freeze silently blocks valid submits
findings.expected_result: Api-mode submit gates read the SERVER's settings, not advisory localStorage. Two bugs to close: the dead freeze preview, and a stale local freeze silently blocking submits.

findings.title: The SPA has no DOM/interaction testing; ~25 test files pin UI by source-string inspection
findings.expected_result: The SPA gets interaction testing, OR a written decision that it will not. NOTE R-22: this repo has NO jsdom and `test/standalone.test.ts` enforces a dependency allowlist — 'add jsdom' is a real architectural change, not a dependency bump.

findings.title: GitHub App credential fetches have no timeout, and any failure terminally fails the scan job with no retry
findings.expected_result: GitHub App credential fetches have a timeout, and a transient failure stops terminally failing the scan job with no retry.

findings.title: Drift-upload compensation is non-transactional best-effort
findings.expected_result: Drift-upload compensation stops being non-transactional best-effort, or its limits are stated and bounded.

findings.title: `drift-edit` writes are neither atomic nor transactional: a mid-batch refusal leaves earlier edits in the checkout
findings.expected_result: `drift-edit` writes become atomic/transactional: a mid-batch refusal leaves NO earlier edits in the checkout.

findings.title: Unexpected errors become `{code:'INTERNAL'}` 500 with zero server-side logging

findings.title: Failed atomic writes leak temp files in the store path

findings.title: Request-status vocabulary is three-way inconsistent (SPA union vs server writes vs YAML prose)

findings.expected_result: The scanner service has a healthcheck and stops exiting on any control-plane error.

findings.title: `prepare()` leaks the cloned workspace when `rev-parse` fails

findings.title: Session rows are still written with blind full-row puts

findings.title: The documented CI-runner cutover only routes 2 of 8 workflows

findings.expected_result: Push-trigger path filters include the workflow file itself on ccp-api and ccp-smoke. EXTEND `scripts/ci/check-path-filters.sh` so it catches this class.

findings.title: Golden-tree comparison is one-directional: extra files created by an edit go unnoticed
findings.expected_result: Golden-tree comparison is bidirectional: extra files created by an edit are reported.

findings.title: One test file consumes ~60% of the api suite wall time by rebuilding catalogctl per run

findings.title: Sleep-based synchronization in async API tests (flake and false-pass risk)
findings.expected_result: Async API tests synchronize on a condition, not a sleep.

findings.title: Functional test plan drift: stale counts, loose citations, and "new" rows with no tracking
findings.expected_result: The functional test plan's counts and citations match HEAD, and 'new' rows are tracked.
